headline: Computational models link actomyosin filament mechanics and turnover to force transmission and tissue form
label: Mechanics Driven Cytoskeletal Force Models
summary: Four November 2026 preprints apply mechanistic actomyosin models from cortex and perinuclear actin to cell contacts and wing disc morphogenesis.
synthesis: The shared thread is that actomyosin and filament mechanics, including turnover, strain-dependent depolymerization and myosin activity, are modeled explicitly to explain how force is organized across scales. A discrete cortex model reconstructs local surface stress from element forces to identify dynamic load-bearing structures. A physics-based actin network model attributes perinuclear actin structures to mechanosensitive polymerization. The Fourier Contour Cell study connects deformability and self-propulsion to bimodal intercellular contact-force distributions. The Drosophila MORPHIOME framework extends this to tissue scale, calibrating a multiscale model with imaging data to resolve the mechanical sequence of wing disc eversion, including ECM. The previous claim that none reports experimental comparison no longer holds, since the wing study uses imaging calibration.
